text:
jia: Quick check — do folks prefer a tiny REST front that proxies to gRPC/proto backends, or do we go proto-first with an opinionated gateway? Thinking about quota propagation, telemetry fidelity, and console UX for rollouts. :thinking:

omar: +1 proto-first for internal services. better type safety and fewer transcoding bugs. but client ergonomics for web apps suffer.

kevin: We need to decide by Thursday. Main tradeoffs: 1) telemetry: direct gRPC -> richer spans/metrics; 2) quotas: header vs claim propagation; 3) console UX: how to show per-route token cost if we transcode.

sara: FWIW, ops wants consistent per-route quotas in the console. If we put a REST shim, we must ensure it doesn't swallow route metadata.

anne: Can we do a hybrid: proto-first + small hostable web SDK that does the JSON <-> proto conversion client-side? That preserves telemetry upstream and keeps web ergonomics.

jia: hybrid sounds plausible. question: how do we propagate quota keys? Example header approach: ```
X-Quota-User: user:123
X-Quota-Route: embed.create.v2
```
but brittle if proxies strip headers.

kevin: Alternative: encode route claim into signed JWT in Authorization metadata so gRPC and REST gateway can verify. pros: can't be easily stripped. cons: rollout UX — console needs to mint/rotate claims.

omar: Signed claims are safer. Also helps in smart routing for Dedicated/private deployments where we must enforce per-tenant limits at runtime.

deploy-bot: deploy started: gateway/proto-gateway:v2 -> canary -> 5%

jia: If we go signed claims, console needs a 'mint claim' button + API to request short-lived route tokens. That ties into billing and per-route cost metrics.

kevin: Telemetry: ensure we carry traceparent and route-id as distinct fields. For gRPC we can use metadata: `traceparent`, `x-route-id`. For REST shim, ensure it sets `x-route-id` header before proxying. Agent note: add a test that asserts `x-route-id` present in spans.

omar: For rollout UX, canary should include signal: token-cost delta, 50p/95p latency, and quality regressions from eval set. Console should show these in one small card.

anne: Also add a slow-path fallback: if mismatch in claims or missing quota header, gateway should return 412 with reason and a link to docs: https://internal.redwood/ops/protocols#claims

jia: Action items: 1) kevin/omar prototype signed-claim flow + sample client (node/python) 2) anne flesh out console minting UX + canary signals 3) sara verify proxy header passthrough policy in infra (NGINX/envoy). Will sync Fri 11am. :rocket:
